caveats: Axon release notes describe platform capability and availability, not Syracuse's enabled tenant settings.
The opt-in routing capability does not prove Syracuse disabled Evidence.com ALPR Fleet Search or routes every ALPR search through Fusus.
Permission-gated add-to-hotlist capability does not identify Syracuse hotlists, users, approvers, or alert routing.
No Flock-to-Axon migration, coexistence, user, hotlist, device, or sharing edge is inferred from this release.

conclusions: Axon Fusus 2026.31 adds a concrete audit-governance control relevant to #2100: an agency can opt to make Fusus the single ALPR search surface and thereby standardize capture of Case Number, Offense Category, and Reason for search.
The same release makes adding a plate to a hotlist directly from ALPR search results permission-gated, tightening the native-record target for hotlist provenance and authorization.

For Syracuse, these capabilities define specific configuration questions rather than configured facts: whether the opt-in routing is enabled, which permissions allow hotlist mutation, and what the audit record shows for searches and hotlist changes remain unresolved.
counterarguments: A product option may be available without being enabled by Syracuse; only tenant configuration or audit evidence can establish deployment state.
A consistent Fusus audit trail does not itself prove completeness across prior Evidence.com searches, third-party sources, or pre-enable activity.
findings: Axon Fusus 2026.31, scheduled for August 31, 2026, allows authorized users to add license plates directly to a hotlist from ALPR search table, card, and detail views; access is controlled by account permissions.
Axon Fusus 2026.31 introduces an opt-in agency capability to turn off the ALPR Fleet Search tab in Evidence.com and route users to Fusus LPR Search.

Axon states that Fusus LPR Search captures Case Number, Offense Category, and Reason for search, and frames the opt-in consolidation as a way to produce a consistent audit trail and document search purpose.
The release notes state the single-search-surface option is opt-in and available in US1; they do not identify which agencies have enabled it.
data.framework: ALPR source/device → search entry point → required purpose fields → user permission → hotlist mutation → audit event; Syracuse enablement and any Flock continuity remain separate predicates.
limitations: No Syracuse tenant screenshot/export, search-settings record, role export, hotlist record, or audit export was recovered in this pass.
The release notes do not establish historical coverage before an agency enables the optional Fusus-only search route.
